content: 1. The Inter-agency Field Manual on Reproductive Health in Humanitarian Settings provides comprehensive guidance on addressing reproductive health needs in crisis situations. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 2. The Consolidated Guidelines on the Use of Antiretroviral Drugs for Treating and Preventing HIV Infection offers evidence-based recommendations for a public health approach to HIV management. This second edition was accessed on August 25, 2021. 3. A study by Zachariah et al. (2002) highlights that moderate to severe malnutrition in tuberculosis patients significantly increases the risk of early mortality. This was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 4. The Guideline: Updates on the Management of Severe Acute Malnutrition in Infants and Children provides updated protocols for treating malnutrition in vulnerable pediatric populations. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 5. The WHO and UNICEF joint statement on Child Growth Standards and the Identification of Severe Acute Malnutrition in Infants and Children outlines criteria for diagnosing and managing malnutrition. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 6. Davies et al. (2006) explored the epidemiological association and immunopathogenesis of smoking and tuberculosis, emphasizing the detrimental effects of tobacco use on TB outcomes. This was published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 7. The Diagnosis and Management of Type 2 Diabetes (HEARTS-D) document provides clinical guidance for managing diabetes in various settings. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 8. The mhGAP Humanitarian Intervention Guide (mhGAP-HIG) focuses on the clinical management of mental, neurological, and substance use conditions in humanitarian emergencies. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 9. Alene et al. (2018) conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the impact of mental health disorders, social stressors, and health-related quality of life in patients with multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. This was published in the Journal of Infection. 10. Lönnroth et al. (2008) systematically reviewed the role of alcohol use as a risk factor for tuberculosis, emphasizing its contribution to TB burden. This was published in BMC Public Health. 11. Getahun et al. (2013) discussed strategies for managing tuberculosis in individuals who use and inject illicit drugs, highlighting the challenges and solutions in this population. This was published in the Bulletin of the World Health Organization. 12. The Alcohol, Smoking, and Substance Involvement Screening Test (ASSIST) manual provides a tool for primary care providers to screen for substance use disorders. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 13. The Consolidated Guidelines on HIV Prevention, Diagnosis, Treatment, and Care for Key Populations (2016 update) offers targeted recommendations for addressing HIV in high-risk groups. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 14. The WHO guidelines on integrating collaborative TB and HIV services within a comprehensive care package for people who inject drugs emphasize the importance of coordinated care. This was accessed on August 25, 2021. 15. Bissell et al. (2016) provided evidence-based recommendations for smoking cessation and creating smoke-free environments for tuberculosis patients. This was published in the second edition of their guidelines. 16. The WHO document on prioritizing diseases for research and development in emergency contexts outlines a framework for addressing health challenges in crises. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 17. Qiu et al. (2020) analyzed the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic on health, culture, and society, emphasizing its far-reaching consequences. This was published in the journal Health, Culture, and Society. 18. The WHO report on the Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on TB Detection and Mortality in 2020 highlights the disruptions caused by the pandemic on tuberculosis control efforts. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 19. The Interim Guidance on Public Health and Social Measures for COVID-19 Preparedness and Response in Low-Capacity and Humanitarian Settings provides actionable recommendations for managing COVID-19 in resource-limited environments. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 20. The WHO guidance on Preparedness, Prevention, and Control of Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19) for Refugees and Migrants in Non-Camp Settings addresses the unique challenges faced by displaced populations. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 21. The Interim Guidance: Scaling-Up COVID-19 Outbreak Readiness and Response Operations in Humanitarian Situations offers strategies for managing outbreaks in camps and camp-like settings. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 22. The WHO End TB Strategy outlines global targets and strategies for tuberculosis prevention, care, and control beyond 2015. It was accessed on August 3, 2021. 23. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 2: Screening, provides guidance on systematic screening for TB disease. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 24. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 1: Prevention, focuses on tuberculosis preventive treatment strategies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 25. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 3: Diagnosis, emphasizes the use of rapid diagnostics for TB detection. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 26. The WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis, Module 4: Treatment, provides updated recommendations for managing drug-resistant tuberculosis. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 27. The WHO guidelines on tuberculosis infection prevention and control (2019 update) offer evidence-based measures to reduce TB transmission. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 28. The WHO position paper on BCG vaccines (February 2018) provides recommendations on the use of Bacillus Calmette-Guérin vaccines for TB prevention. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 29. The WHO Public-Private Mix for TB Prevention and Care: A Roadmap outlines strategies for engaging private sector stakeholders in TB control efforts. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 30. The WHO guidelines for the treatment of drug-susceptible tuberculosis and patient care (2017 update) provide evidence-based recommendations for managing TB. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 31. The WHO ethics guidance for implementing the End TB Strategy emphasizes the importance of ethical considerations in TB control programs. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 32. The Global Laboratory Initiative: Practical Guide to TB Laboratory Strengthening provides technical guidance for improving TB diagnostic capacity. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 33. The WHO summary on Chest Radiography in Tuberculosis Detection highlights current recommendations and programmatic approaches for using radiography in TB diagnosis. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 34. The WHO Toolkit to Develop a National Strategic Plan for TB Prevention, Care, and Control provides a methodology for creating effective national TB strategies. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 35. The WHO guidelines for managing tuberculosis in children (second edition) provide specific recommendations for pediatric TB care. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 36. The WHO framework for conducting reviews of tuberculosis programs offers a structured approach to evaluating TB control efforts. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 37. The WHO Guideline: Nutritional Care and Support for Patients with Tuberculosis emphasizes the role of nutrition in TB treatment outcomes. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 38. The WHO policy on collaborative TB/HIV activities provides guidelines for integrating TB and HIV services at the national level. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 39. The WHO manual on electronic recording and reporting for tuberculosis care and control outlines best practices for digital data management in TB programs. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 40. The WHO Tuberculosis Laboratory Biosafety Manual provides guidance on ensuring safety in TB diagnostic laboratories. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 41. The WHO ENGAGE-TB Approach: Operational Guidance promotes community-based TB activities to enhance TB prevention and care. It was accessed on August 25, 2021. 42. The WHO/Union monograph on TB and tobacco control highlights the intersection of these two global epidemics and the need for integrated control efforts. It was accessed on August 25, 2021.
